lines.text: Pip stumbles down the harbor steps and sits on a bollard, clutching the trumpet case like a life jacket.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: (I ran from the police. Me. I once apologized to a vending machine.)
Across the water, every loudspeaker in Port Murmur crackles to life at once.

lines.speaker: quill
lines.text: Citizens! This is Mayor Prudence Quill. Day one of the Silence Act has been a triumph of tranquility.

lines.speaker: quill
lines.text: Regrettably, one trumpeter resisted. Remember: quiet is a public good. Report loud neighbors to the Quiet Squad.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: (Gus will get fined. Maybe the dancing toddler too. All because I couldn't just not play.)
A woman in a long red coat sits down on the next bollard. Every one of her rings is shaped like a tiny brass horn.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: Nice getaway, kid. Most people in this town run from the music. You ran with it.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Oh. Um, thanks? It was less a getaway and more a panic with a direction.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: The Squad has your face now. Your corner days are over.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: (So that's it. No corner, no song. Back to practicing in the bathroom with a towel over the bell.)

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: Unless you play where the meters can't reach. Under the old fish auction there's a door with no handle. Knock twice and hum a B-flat.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: Only if they hear you. Ask for Ruby at the Brass Cellar.
When Pip looks up, the bollard is empty. Somewhere under the street, very faintly, a tuba plays one long note.
